claims.statement: Stripe's current Polish standard pricing lists a 90 PLN dispute-received fee, a separate 90 PLN manually countered fee that is returned on a win, and Smart Disputes at 30% of recovered disputed value.
Stripe already supplies processor-native AI-prepared dispute evidence and outcome pricing, so a Stripe-only evidence pack is not a differentiated wedge.

Stripe says merchants usually have 7-21 days to respond, issuer review usually takes 60-75 days, and the full lifecycle normally takes 2-3 months; recovered funds therefore cannot support immediate vendor cash collection.
Stripe Apps require explicit object-level permissions, and the signed-in user also needs access; merchant data and submission rights cannot be assumed merely because an app is installed.

Adyen exposes retrieval of applicable defense reasons, evidence-document upload or deletion, and accept-or-defend actions, but requires an API key with the dispute-management role, webhooks, and an online-payments integration; not every dispute is defendable.

Processor and network timing is heterogeneous: Adyen documents chargeback-response windows of 18 days for Visa outside the shortened US/Canada case and 40 days for Mastercard, with typical final-decision windows of 45-70 days after defense; PSP deadlines can be shorter than network maxima.
Shopify already collects evidence, sends it on the due date, and adds AI-generated insights for product-not-received disputes, further shrinking the wedge for ordinary Shopify Payments merchants.

Chargeflow currently advertises end-to-end evidence collection and submission across more than 100 integrations for 25% of recovered chargeback value, with no charge on losses; its integration-count and performance claims are vendor claims, not independent validation.

Mastercard's sponsored 2025 report gives average chargeback values of $120 for travel and hospitality, $84 for retail, $77 for digital goods, and $69 for subscriptions, while 16% of merchant chargebacks in its sample were low-dollar write-offs; modest values constrain success-fee revenue per reviewed case.

The Mastercard report is based on 840 midsize and large merchants in the US, UK, Brazil, and Australia and explicitly says the data are third-party research rather than Mastercard transactions, so it does not establish a CEE value or volume distribution.

In the MRC/Cybersource survey, European respondents reported a 15.1% trimmed-average annual win rate for fraud-coded chargebacks and disputes, and only 43% of European respondents reported monitoring at the refund/dispute stage; this suggests a process gap but not incremental vendor lift.

Visa's VAMP formula counts reported fraud and disputes and explicitly excludes specified pre-dispute resolutions and qualifying Compelling Evidence 3.0 fraud; ordinary successful representment is not listed as an exclusion, so recovery work generally does not solve the merchant's monitoring-ratio problem.

GDPR purpose limitation, data minimization, storage limitation, security, and processor-contract duties mean cross-merchant reuse of order, device, support, and outcome data needs a defined legal role and basis; pseudonymization alone does not automatically make the corpus reusable as anonymous data.

Shopify's official directory currently exposes 37 partners in Poland, creating a finite, reachable channel-test list, but it does not reveal which partners serve merchants with meaningful dispute volume.

At a 20% recovery fee, 500 PLN average disputed value, and 35% win rate, expected revenue is 35 PLN per reviewed incoming dispute; a 12-minute review at 60 PLN per hour plus 7 PLN of systems and support yields about 46% pilot gross margin, while the MRC Europe win benchmark and a lower value make the model loss-making.

No accessed authoritative source establishes how many reachable Polish or CEE merchants simultaneously use multiple PSPs, receive at least 50 defendable disputes per month, and have at least 500 PLN average disputed value.

No independent evidence establishes incremental win-rate lift or labor reduction from this proposed reviewed cross-processor layer versus the same merchant's native Stripe, Adyen, Shopify, or incumbent-vendor workflow.

Outcome labels do not by themselves form a moat: major processors and incumbents already observe larger outcome corpora, while GDPR and merchant contracts can prevent reuse of raw cross-merchant evidence.

contrary_evidence: Processor-native and platform-native automation already covers ordinary Stripe and Shopify merchants.
Chargeflow directly offers cross-processor evidence collection and submission at 25% of wins across more than 100 claimed integrations.
Typical reported digital and subscription dispute values are below the proposed 500 PLN gate, while Europe's reported fraud-coded win benchmark makes reviewed outcome-only delivery uneconomic.
Representment recovery does not generally fix the dispute-count monitoring problem, so prevention products can own the higher-priority budget.
Cross-merchant data reuse is legally and contractually constrained and larger processors and incumbents already have more outcome data.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the 37-company Polish Shopify partner directory as a finite pilot channel, plus targeted outreach to CEE payments and fraud leads. Planning CAC is 3,000 PLN per qualified merchant: 1,000 PLN paid referral after the volume gate and 2,000 PLN equivalent founder qualification and onboarding effort. Neither conversion nor CAC is evidenced.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Not a validated base case. Conditional bootstrap path with 85% founder ownership and no debt: year 1, 5 merchants at 50 cases per month produce about 105,000 PLN annual revenue; while employed, reinvest 95% of after-tax cash and distribute no more than 5%. Year 2, 30 merchants produce 630,000 PLN revenue at 60% gross margin and 10% EBITDA; only then consider leaving employment after securing 12 months of runway. Year 3, 100 merchants produce 2.10 million PLN revenue and 20% EBITDA. Year 5, 250 merchants produce 5.25 million PLN revenue and 25% EBITDA; at 4x EBITDA the business is worth 5.25 million PLN and the founder's 85% equity is 4.46 million PLN, with retained earnings not counted again as personal cash. Year 6, 350 merchants produce 7.35 million PLN revenue and 28% EBITDA; 4x EBITDA implies 8.23 million PLN business value and about 7.0 million PLN founder equity, crossing the 5 million PLN definition. This path fails if the volume, value, win-rate, CAC, retention, ownership, margin, or valuation assumptions fail, and no CEE evidence currently supports the required merchant count.
economics.founder_time: Months 0-6 require 3.5-5 hours per day, capped at 150 cases per month: about 30 monthly review hours at 12 minutes per case plus integration, security, buyer interviews, and partner outreach. Above 500 cases per month, hire and train QA rather than expanding founder labor. Keep the corporate job until positive contribution economics, repeatable demand, objective traction, and at least 12 months of personal runway are all demonstrated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Conservative gate model per 100 reviewed disputes: 500 PLN average value x 35% wins x 20% fee = 3,500 PLN revenue. Pilot delivery at 12 review minutes per case and 60 PLN loaded hourly cost is 1,200 PLN, plus 700 PLN data, hosting, and support, producing 1,600 PLN gross profit and 46% gross margin. Mature delivery at six review minutes costs 600 PLN plus the same 700 PLN, producing 2,200 PLN gross profit and 63% gross margin. At the MRC Europe 15.1% win benchmark and a 320 PLN planning value, revenue is only about 966 PLN per 100 cases, below pilot delivery cost.
economics.payback: At the minimum gate of 50 monthly cases, 500 PLN average value, 35% wins, and 20% fee, recognized monthly revenue is 1,750 PLN. At 63% mature gross margin, monthly gross profit is about 1,103 PLN and a 3,000 PLN CAC pays back in 2.7 recognized-revenue months; adding the documented 2-3 month outcome lag makes cash payback roughly 5-6 months. Pilot-margin cash payback is longer.
economics.pricing: Pilot proposal: 20% of recovered principal, charged only after the issuer decision is final and recovered funds return; no setup or monthly fee. This undercuts Chargeflow's 25% and Stripe Smart Disputes' 30%, but is modeled only for merchants with at least 50 disputes per month and at least 500 PLN average disputed value.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Disputes recur monthly, but outcome-only revenue falls if prevention works, volume shifts, or the merchant adopts a native or incumbent tool. The planning case assumes 80% annual logo retention and no minimum contract; this is unvalidated and must be measured over 12 months.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Merchant-specific templates plus aggregate reason, evidence, and outcome statistics built only from contractually permitted, minimized, genuinely de-identified data. Do not claim a cross-merchant model-training moat until legal reuse, irreversibility of anonymization, and independent incremental lift are proven.
fingerprint.customer: Polish and CEE online travel, ticketing, and digital-service merchants using at least two PSPs, with at least 50 defendable disputes per month, at least 500 PLN average disputed value, and documented evidence gaps beyond native PSP or commerce-platform packets.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Recruit data donors through the 37 Shopify partners listed in Poland and targeted CEE payment or fraud leaders; pay a referral only after a merchant meets the volume and value gates. Exclude ordinary Shopify-only merchants already served by native evidence automation unless they have non-Shopify PSPs or verified evidence gaps.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A read-only cross-PSP intake and ROI triage layer that gathers missing evidence, builds a reason-code-specific packet, applies a six-minute target human QA and merchant approval, submits through merchant-authorized processor access, reconciles outcomes, and reports preventable root causes. Begin in shadow mode and do not auto-submit until prospective lift is proven.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The head of payments or fraud, finance lead, COO, or owner pays 20% of recovered principal only after the issuer's final decision and return of funds. The service contests only cases whose expected recovery exceeds processor fees, review cost, and error risk.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A chargeback debits the transaction and fee, creates a processor-specific response deadline often inside 7-21 days, and requires evidence scattered across payment, fulfillment, application-usage, and support systems; a favorable outcome usually arrives 60-75 days later and generally does not erase monitoring-ratio impact.

founder_fit: The integrations, evidence classification, measurement, and ROI triage fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage.
A capped shadow pilot can run part-time and without camera-led distribution, but scaled human review, security, and enterprise trust are poor fits unless hired out after objective traction.
The official Polish partner list gives a bounded low-social-energy outreach experiment, though enterprise payment leaders will still require high-trust sales and diligence.
The 100,000 PLN available capital can fund a narrow pilot, but not prolonged multi-PSP integration and manual operations without paid validation.
risks: A late, incorrect, or overbroad one-shot submission can destroy rather than create recovery value.
Success fees can be disputed if attribution is unclear or a case would have been won natively.
Processor terms, permissions, or APIs can change and eliminate submission access.
Two-to-three-month outcomes create receivables and working-capital exposure.
Native tools and incumbents can bundle equivalent features or undercut a narrow CEE entrant.
Personal data in order, device, support, and outcome records creates breach, contract, and GDPR exposure.
Outcome data may improve operations but does not automatically become a defensible or lawfully reusable moat.
The founder's part-time constraint is incompatible with unbounded manual review or enterprise onboarding.
thesis: This is viable only as a tightly gated recovery service for CEE merchants whose native processor or platform packets demonstrably omit material application-usage, fulfillment, or customer-communication evidence. It should not be built as generic chargeback automation: require multiple PSPs, at least 50 defendable disputes per month, at least 500 PLN average disputed value, a blind incremental-lift result, merchant approval, and positive net-dollar recovery after processor and review costs.
title: Reviewed multi-processor dispute recovery for high-AOV CEE digital and travel merchants
uncertainties: Existence and count of CEE merchants that meet every proposed volume, value, multi-PSP, and evidence-gap gate.
Blind lift against each merchant's native workflow and the causal source of any lift.
Real manual-review minutes, submission error rate, support load, and reviewer training cost.
Merchant-granted submission rights and acceptable commercial terms for every target PSP.
Actual CAC, partner referral rate, buyer authority, sales cycle, and 12-month retention.
Whether privacy-safe aggregates remain useful after removing personal and merchant-identifying detail.
Whether the CEE market alone can support the merchant count required by the founder wealth path.
